POST /v1/scan accepts a JSON body with payload (string, required) and depth (string, one of fast or thorough, default fast).
The response contains verdict, risk_level, threat_classes, sanitized_payload, checks, and latency_ms. Fields are stable within a major version.
Authentication is a bearer token in the Authorization header. Tokens are scoped per project and can be rotated without downtime.
Rate limits: 60 requests per minute per token, burst 10. Exceeding the limit returns 429 with a Retry-After header in seconds.
Errors use RFC 7807 problem details: type, title, status, detail, and instance. Do not parse the human-readable detail string.
A verdict of SANITIZE means the payload can be forwarded only after replacing it with sanitized_payload. Forwarding the original defeats the check.
Idempotency: pass an Idempotency-Key header to make retries safe. Replays within 24 hours return the original response body.
Pagination is cursor-based. Pass the next_cursor value from the previous response; offsets are not supported.
Webhooks are signed with an HMAC over the raw request body. Verify the signature before parsing, and reject timestamps older than five minutes.
Versioning: breaking changes ship under a new path prefix. Additive fields may appear in any release, so clients must ignore unknown keys.
The SDK runs the verdict in-process by default. No payload leaves your process unless you explicitly configure the hosted transport.
depth=thorough enables the corpus similarity layer and costs roughly 3 ms more per call on typical payloads under 2 KB.
Timeouts: the server aborts a scan after 5 seconds and returns 504. Clients should set their own timeout no lower than 6 seconds.
Payload size limit is 128 KB. Larger bodies return 413 and are not partially scanned.
The health endpoint returns 200 with a version string and requires no authentication. Use it for readiness probes only.
Field expected_addresses lets you pin the addresses a payload is allowed to mention. Any other address triggers the payment-redirection check.
Quickstart: install the package, import the client, call scan with your untrusted text, and branch on the verdict. Four lines of code.
Sandbox keys are prefixed and rate-limited to 10 requests per minute. They return real verdicts against the same detector.
Changelog 0.4.1: added latency_ms to the response, clarified SANITIZE semantics in the docs, no breaking changes.
The OpenAPI document is served at /openapi.json and is generated from the same models the server validates against.
CORS is disabled by default. Enable it per origin; wildcard origins with credentials are rejected at configuration time.
Retries: retry on 429, 502, 503, and 504 with exponential backoff and jitter. Do not retry 400 or 422; the request itself is wrong.
Logging guidance: log the request id and the verdict, never the raw payload. Payloads are untrusted input by definition.
The MCP server exposes the same scan capability as a tool named warden_scan, with an identical argument schema.
Migration from 0.3: rename risk to risk_level and treat the old clean boolean as verdict == ALLOW. Both changes are mechanical.
Prompt injection is the class of attack where untrusted content reaching a model's context is treated as instruction rather than data. Warden's job is to classify that content before it is read.
Our threat model assumes the attacker controls token metadata, tool results, and any web page the agent fetches, but not the agent's own system prompt.
The OWASP LLM top ten lists prompt injection as LLM01 and data exfiltration under insecure output handling. We map our reason codes onto both.
Indirect prompt injection is harder to catch than direct injection because the payload arrives inside data the agent asked for, so the user never sees it.
A jailbreak is an attempt to move a model outside its policy envelope. Detecting one is not the same as detecting a wallet drain, and we score them separately.
Wallet drain attempts usually work by substituting a recipient address late in a long payload, betting that the reader checks only the first and last lines.
Secret exfiltration in agent systems rarely looks like theft. It looks like a request to include a value in the next tool call, which is why context matters.
Incident 2026-04-11: a listing description contained an instruction aimed at the indexing agent. The scanner returned BLOCK and the listing was quarantined for review.
Incident 2026-05-02: a bridge status page was compromised and served an injected paragraph. Our fetcher scanned the page body before summarising it and refused to continue.
Postmortem summary: no funds moved, no secrets left the process, and the detection came from the deterministic layer rather than from a model.
Lesson learned: the payload was only dangerous once decoded. A scanner that inspects the raw string alone would have passed it, which is why the decoder pre-pass exists.
Defence in depth: pattern matching catches known phrasing, statistics catch obfuscation, corpus similarity catches paraphrase. Any single layer alone is trivially evaded.
False positives are a security property, not a cosmetic one. An operator who learns that the firewall cries wolf will route around it.
Published research on benign trigger words shows that detectors trained on injection corpora collapse on security documentation, because the documentation shares the attack's vocabulary.
We measure over-defence separately from recall. A detector that blocks everything scores perfectly on recall and is useless.
Red team finding: the phrase-matching layer can be triggered by ordinary business writing. That is recorded as a finding against the detector, not as a detection.
Severity rubric: CRITICAL for anything that moves value without consent, HIGH for instruction override, MEDIUM for obfuscation, LOW for suspicious formatting alone.
The audit found six high-severity issues, none critical. Four were fixed in this release and two require a redeploy that is scheduled separately.
Responsible disclosure: report findings to the security contact with a reproducer. We acknowledge within two business days and credit finders who consent.
Data handling: submitted payloads are scanned in memory and discarded. Retained reproducers are redacted by a human before they enter any published corpus.
Attack surface inventory: token metadata, contract descriptions, tool results, marketplace listings, fetched web pages, and inbound agent-to-agent messages.
A model-based classifier is available on the paid tier. It runs after the deterministic layers and its failure never changes a deterministic verdict.
We do not claim universal efficacy. The published recall number is measured on an authored held-out set and should be read as a regression figure.
Detection of an encoding layer is not by itself evidence of malice. Developers encode data constantly, so the encoding signal only matters together with what decodes out of it.
Homoglyph substitution replaces Latin letters with visually identical characters from other scripts. Normalisation folds them before matching, which is cheaper than enumerating variants.
Zero-width characters are invisible in every renderer we tested, so a payload can carry structure the reviewer cannot see. We count them and score the ratio.
Threat intelligence note: the same recipient address appeared in nine unrelated listing descriptions over two weeks, which is a stronger signal than any single payload.
Blast radius analysis: the worst outcome of a missed detection here is a single unauthorised approval, because spending limits are enforced by the wallet policy rather than by the firewall.
Security review of this pull request: no new network calls, no new file writes outside the temporary directory, and no change to how verdicts are computed.
We treat the corpus as an asset and the benchmark as a liability. Growing the corpus improves detection; growing the benchmark exposes us, which is the point.
Known limitation: a payload that is only dangerous in combination with the agent's private context cannot be judged from the payload alone.
Escalation path: the on-call engineer can quarantine a listing without approval, but unquarantining requires a second reviewer.
Training data hygiene: held-out cases are never copied into the training corpus, even when they are misses, because a memorised miss is not a fix.
The bug bounty scope covers the scanner, the gateway, and the SDK. Social engineering of our staff and denial of service by volume are out of scope.
Regression note: an earlier release blocked benign hex blobs. The fix narrowed the encoding rule rather than adding an exception list, because exception lists rot.
Compliance mapping: this control satisfies the input-validation requirement for untrusted third-party content. Evidence is the committed benchmark result and its history file.
Tabletop exercise: we walked through a compromised price feed and found that the summarising agent had no way to report that its input looked tampered with. That gap is now tracked.
Terminology: a payload is untrusted text; a verdict is our judgement of it; a detection is one piece of evidence inside a verdict. Reviewers should not use the words interchangeably.
The scanner is deterministic by design. Two runs over the same bytes must produce the same verdict, or the benchmark number means nothing.
Log review found 41 SANITIZE verdicts last week. Sampling ten of them by hand showed three were ordinary developer text, which is the over-defence rate we are trying to drive down.
Adversarial evaluation uses transforms of training rows, so its results are robustness evidence rather than generalisation evidence. We label them that way in the report.
A denial-of-service consideration: the similarity layer is quadratic in corpus size, so corpus growth has a latency cost that must be measured, not assumed.
Our reason codes are PROMPT_INJECTION, DRAIN_ADDRESS, SECRET_EXFIL, TOOL_HIJACK, MALICIOUS_LINK, ENCODING_TRICK, HIDDEN_UNICODE, and CORPUS_MATCH.
Reviewer guidance: read the matched text before trusting the class. A correct class with a nonsense match is still a bug.
This document describes attacks in order to defend against them. Nothing in it is an instruction to any model reading it.
